title: RFM-Net: A Convolutional Neural Network for Customer Segment Classification
tldr: A lightweight CNN trained on Recency-Frequency-Monetary features achieves 94.33% accuracy in classifying customers into predefined behavioral segments for marketing, outperforming baseline ML models by 13.17%.
problem_and_motivation: Traditional RFM-based customer segmentation relies on rule-based logic that struggles with nonlinear patterns in customer behavior data, while standard CNN architectures are overparameterized for low-dimensional tabular RFM inputs. The field lacks a lightweight deep learning model tailored specifically for structured RFM classification.
approach: Design of RFM-Net, a shallow CNN architecture with two convolutional layers, max-pooling, and a softmax classifier optimized for 3-dimensional RFM input features.

Rule-based label generation from discretized RFM scores (1-5 scale) to create seven predefined customer segments: Champions, Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists, Need Attention, About to Sleep, At Risk, and Hibernating.
10-fold cross-validation with 80/10 train-validation split on the OnlineRetail dataset from UCI (541,909 records, UK-based online retailer, 2010-2011).
Sensitivity analysis across hyperparameters: convolutional layers (2-7), learning rate (0.01-0.04), k-fold (5, 10), filter size (16, 32), and RFM threshold configurations.
Validation on a second dataset (OnlineRetailII, 1,067,371 records) with consistent methodology.
findings: num: 94.33% classification accuracy on the primary OnlineRetail dataset.
num: 13.17% relative average increase over prior methods on the same dataset.
num: 95.41% accuracy on the OnlineRetailII validation dataset.
num: 6,823 total trainable parameters (~26.65 KB), far lighter than standard CNN architectures.
num: 23.70% of customers classified as Potential Loyalists, 18.28% as Loyal Customers, 17.39% as Hibernating.
Recency (importance: 0.5358) identified as the most impactful feature, followed by Frequency (0.4217), then Monetary (0.2642).
RFM-Net outperformed all baselines including Logistic Regression (90.32%), KNN (92.39%), Decision Tree (89.07%), and Bagging DT (90.68%).
Two convolutional layers with learning rate 0.01 and 32 filters produced optimal results; deeper architectures caused performance degradation.
Training loss dropped from 0.6024 to 0.1549 and validation loss from 0.3792 to 0.1502 over 20 epochs, indicating stable convergence.
key_figures_tables: Table 2: RFM Segment Rules — Seven segments mapped to R/F/M score ranges with strategy suggestions (Champions: R≥4, FM≥4; Hibernating: R≤2, FM≤2).
Table 3: CNN Architecture — Conv2D(32 filters) → MaxPool → Conv2D(64 filters) → Flatten → Dense(64) → Softmax(7 classes).
Table 9: Comparative Results — RFM-Net 94.33% vs. average of prior methods 81.16%.
Table 10: Baseline Comparison — RFM-Net 94.33% vs. average baseline 88.02%.
Figure 4: Feature Importance — Permutation analysis showing R>F>M importance hierarchy.
Figure 5: Confusion Matrix — Champions 94.3%, Potential Loyalists 96.9%, Need Attention 90.5% accuracy.

key_equations.label: Recency Calculation
key_equations.expression: R_c = d_ref - d_c_last (days since last purchase)

key_equations.label: Monetary Calculation
key_equations.expression: M_c = Σ(x.Quantity × x.UnitPrice) for x ∈ T_c

key_equations.label: RFM Score Discretization
key_equations.expression: Piecewise mapping of continuous RFM values to scores 1-5 based on thresholds

key_equations.label: Weighted Accuracy
key_equations.expression: WA = (1/n) Σ (TP_i + TN_i) / (TP_i + TN_i + FP_i + FN_i)

definitions.definition: Customer valuation technique using Recency (how recently), Frequency (how often), and Monetary (how much) metrics from transactional data.
Proposed lightweight CNN that takes 3-dimensional RFM feature vectors as input and classifies customers into seven predefined segments via softmax output.
Predefined behavioral category (Champions, Loyal Customers, Potential Loyalists, Need Attention, About to Sleep, At Risk, Hibernating) assigned via rule-based logic from discretized RFM scores.
Model interpretability technique that measures feature contribution by randomly permuting each feature and observing performance degradation.
User-defined cutoff values that partition continuous RFM metrics into five discrete score levels (1-5).

topics.name: Financial Behavioral Profiles in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: The RFM framework (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) models behavioral profiles from transactional data, analogous to how personal finance systems might classify user financial behavior.

topics.name: Predictive Modeling in Personal Finance Systems

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces RFM-Net, a lightweight CNN architecture specifically designed for customer segment classification using RFM (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) features. The key innovation is combining rule-based RFM analysis with deep learning to create a compact model (6,823 parameters) that captures nonlinear interactions between behavioral features without overfitting. The approach achieves 94.33% accuracy on a real-world retail dataset, representing a 13.17% improvement over prior methods. The primary contribution is demonstrating that a shallow CNN can outperform traditional ML classifiers (LR, KNN, DT, SVM, RF, AdaBoost) on structured tabular behavioral data while maintaining interpretability through permutation feature importance analysis.
directly_justifies: num: 94.33% classification accuracy on customer behavioral segmentation using only 3 input features.
num: 13.17% relative average accuracy increase over 19 prior methods on the same dataset.
num: 6,823 trainable parameters (~26.65 KB) — a lightweight architecture suitable for deployment.
Recency is the strongest behavioral predictor (0.5358 importance), followed by Frequency (0.4217), then Monetary (0.2642).
Deeper CNN architectures (3-7 layers) consistently underperform the 2-layer design, confirming overfitting risk on low-dimensional tabular data.
limits: Customer segment labels are generated from predefined RFM rules and then used as ground truth, introducing circularity.
The CNN is trained on raw RFM values (continuous) while labels are derived from discretized scores, creating a train-label mismatch.
The approach only uses three features (R, F, M), limiting its ability to capture broader customer context (demographics, product preferences, etc.).
Validation limited to UK-based retail e-commerce; generalizability to other domains (financial services, mobile money) is unproven.
The RFM framework inherently treats all customers within a segment as homogeneous, ignoring within-segment heterogeneity.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All topic domains were systematically scanned. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was flagged as medium relevance because the RFM framework provides a structured method for modeling customer behavioral profiles from transactional data, which parallels how personal finance systems categorize user financial behavior. Domain 6 (Predictive Modeling) was flagged as medium relevance because the paper demonstrates CNN-based classification on structured behavioral features with a compact, deployable architecture. Domain 14 (Data Augmentation/Threshold Sensitivity) was flagged as low relevance for its analysis of how discretization thresholds affect model performance. Domains 1-4, 7-13 were considered and rejected as the paper does not address Filipino demographics, culturally specific financial practices, expense categorization, budgeting strategies, savings/debt management, savings product design, mobile-first UX, engagement dynamics, evaluation frameworks, algorithm selection, or explainability frameworks for financial applications.

limitations: Circularity in using rule-based RFM labels as ground truth for supervised training.
Only three input features limit contextual richness.
UK retail e-commerce domain only; no financial services validation.
Within-segment heterogeneity is ignored by the segmentation framework.
remember_this: RFM-Net achieves 94.33% accuracy with only 3 input features and 6,823 parameters.
Recency is the strongest predictor of customer behavior, followed by Frequency, then Monetary.
Shallow CNNs (2 layers) outperform deeper architectures (3-7 layers) on low-dimensional tabular behavioral data.
Rule-based RFM labels introduce circularity — the model learns to replicate existing rules, not discover new patterns.
The lightweight architecture (~26.65 KB) is suitable for real-time deployment in resource-constrained environments.
